title: Station Meridian Rising Revisited
premise: Zephyrine Eriksen has kept Station Meridian alive for eleven years, the sole human caretaker of an automated relay that carries messages between colonies that have gone silent. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon Wake returns with a crew grown decades younger and memories scrubbed clean, Zephyrine recognizes the ship as the one that carried the massacre survivors everyone else insists never existed. Hunting through corrupted logs, decaying backups, and his own failing memory implants, he uncovers that the colonial authority rewrote history to bury a slaughter—and that the de-aged crew are living proof someone is willing to unmake lives to erase crimes. In the end, Zephyrine broadcasts the truth on the long route, sacrificing the station and his invisibility to give the young crew back their stolen past, choosing justice over survival.
about_author: Theo Blackwood is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent years maintaining remote communications infrastructure in the Arctic before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness, unreliable memory, and the quiet heroism of people the systems forget.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. We meet his solitary routine aboard Station Meridian: repairing ancient relays, talking to the station AI, and logging messages from colonies that stopped answering years ago. The emotional beat is aching loneliness disguised as competence—he has made peace with being the last voice on a dead line, until a proximity alert he hasn't heard in a decade shatters the quiet.

chapters.title: Halcyon, Coming Down
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The ship Halcyon Wake docks, crewed by people who should be in their sixties but are barely twenty-five. Their memories end mid-voyage, decades ago. One of them, a young woman named Ilsa Voss, looks exactly like a passenger manifest Zephyrine remembers from a ship officially lost with all hands. The beat is uncanny dread—the past arriving wearing a younger face.

chapters.title: Records of Nothing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with a fragmentary interlude from Ilsa's recovered dream-memories. He searches the station's deep archives for the Halcyon's original flight plan and finds it scrubbed—cleanly, professionally, by someone with authority-level access. The station AI, Meridian, admits its logs were edited remotely eleven years ago. The beat is the vertigo of realizing his own memory may have been edited too.

chapters.title: What the Crew Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Zephyrine and Ilsa. The de-aged crew fragments into factions: some want to dock at the nearest colony and accept the official story; Ilsa's nightmares of screaming airlocks push her to trust Zephyrine. A quiet bond forms between them over shared insomnia and shared doubt. The beat is fragile trust kindling against mutual isolation.

chapters.title: The Authority Answers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The colonial authority finally responds to his queries: a polite order to stand down, seal the crew aboard, and prepare the Halcyon for 'quarantine retrieval.' A retrieval ship is already en route—six weeks out. Zephyrine realizes his eleven years of invisibility were not neglect but containment. The beat is cold fear: he was never forgotten, he was archived.

chapters.title: Meridian Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV with the station AI Meridian as a second voice. Digging into Meridian's physical backup cores—the one medium too old for remote editing—they recover a partial recording: the Halcyon's distress call from eleven years ago, naming the colony Meridian's sister station as the site of a massacre, and naming the man who ordered it. The beat is grief and fury—the truth exists, but only in rotting tape.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, then Zephyrine's. Ilsa confronts Zephyrine: he knew the Halcyon was lost, he filed the silence away, he chose the station over the truth for eleven years. Their growing love curdles into accusation before hardening into partnership—she will help him only if he stops hiding. Meanwhile the crew loyal to the official story sabotage the backup cores. The beat is love tested by guilt and choosing each other anyway.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The loyalist faction, guided by a planted authority agent among the crew, destroys two of the three backup cores and cripples the station's transmitter. Zephyrine and Ilsa fight through the dark maintenance levels to protect the last tape. Zephyrine is badly injured; Meridian begins shutting down nonessential systems to keep him alive. The beat is desperate sacrifice—the station itself dying so the truth can live.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's and Ilsa's POVs interleaved. With the retrieval ship hours out, they jury-rig the Halcyon's own deep-space array and aim the recovered distress call, the massacre recording, and the crew's de-aging evidence at every colony on the long route. Meridian burns out its final cores to amplify the signal. The retrieval ship arrives to find the truth already loose among the stars. The beat is triumphant, costly defiance—justice screamed into the dark.

chapters.title: Meridian Rising
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, months later. The broadcast forced an inquiry; the architect of the massacre is in custody, and the de-aged crew are recognized as the survivors they always were. Zephyrine, recovering slowly, has lost the station but gained a name, a record, and Ilsa. Together they board a ship on the long route—not running, but carrying the recovered archives home. The beat is bittersweet renewal: survival was the price, and it was worth paying.
